name: hash-blake3-stream
algorithm: std BLAKE3, 32-byte output through the streaming state, fed 1,500-byte pieces (the last piece is the remainder) of splitmix64 bytes, one fresh state per pass, reps passes with a one-byte write-back (mk/hash-blake3-stream.mk).

skip.c: no std hash: C has no standard BLAKE3, 32-byte output
skip.rust: no std BLAKE3, 32-byte output: Rust std has none (only SipHash-1-3 in DefaultHasher); no crate stands in
skip.go: no std BLAKE3, 32-byte output: Go std has none (hash/maphash is a different, seeded hash); no module stands in

notes: Idiomatic standard library, the streaming case (review finding HMR-3): Mk Blake3State.New/Bytes/Sum, Zig init/update/final. 1,500 is not a multiple of the block, so the partial-block path of Bytes runs on every piece. Bytes per second = mib * 1048576 * reps / median.
Zig: std.crypto.hash.Blake3 update hashes whole chunks of a piece in @Vector lanes; Mk is one chunk at a time, scalar.

Checksums: Mk (mk build -release), Zig 0.17.0 (-O ReleaseFast -mcpu=x86_64_v2) and, where it has the function, Go 1.27.3 (GOAMD64=v2 -pgo=off) printed the same quick values on the owner's machine, 2026-11-07 (std-hashmod session 9, HMR-3); the publish-size checksum was agreed by every column in `go run ./tools/bench verify -publish-size`. Not published: no number here is a measurement.
